title: Recarbonizing Global Soils: A Technical Manual of Recommended Management Practices
organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
summary: Demonstrates that legume-based cover crops, compost integration, and reduced tillage increase soil organic carbon (SOC) by 0.15% to 0.40% annually (15-25% cumulative over 3-5 years) in dryland agricultural soils, directly enhancing water holding capacity and soil biological activity.

title: Special Report on Climate Change, Desertification, Land Degradation, Sustainable Land Management, Food Security, and Greenhouse gas fluxes in Terrestrial Ecosystems
summary: Reviews sustainable land management strategies in arid and semi-arid lands, showing that continuous monoculture accelerates soil organic matter depletion by 30-50% and heightens susceptibility to desertification under rainfall deficits below 500 mm/year.

title: Thematic Assessment Report on Pollinators, Pollination and Food Production
organization: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES)
summary: Details the lethal and sublethal impacts of synthetic neonicotinoids and broad-spectrum insecticides on wild pollinators, noting that non-crop wildflower strips, hedgerows, and reducing pesticide frequency restore pollinator visitation rates by 40-70% within 1-2 seasons.

title: Becoming #GenerationRestoration: Ecosystem Restoration for People, Nature and Climate
summary: Synthesizes landscape connectivity studies showing that establishing ecological corridors between fragmented forest patches reduces isolation barriers, increasing gene flow and resident species richness by 20-35% in degraded landscapes.

title: Soil Health Technical Note No. 450-06: Cropping Systems and Water Retention
summary: Finds that every 1% increase in soil organic matter in topsoil increases soil available water capacity by approximately 20,000 gallons per acre (187,000 liters per hectare), mitigating dryland crop moisture stress.

title: Agroforestry in Drylands: Tree-Crop-Soil Interactions and Biodiversity Conservation
summary: Establishes that integrating drought-resilient nitrogen-fixing trees (e.g., Faidherbia albida, Acacia senegal) in dryland cereal cropping moderates microclimate canopy temperatures by 2-4°C, decreases evaporation, and increases mycorrhizal fungi biomass.

title: Water Harvesting and Soil Moisture Conservation for Smallholder Farmers in Semi-Arid Regions
summary: Documents contour bunding, swales, and mulching in semi-arid zones (300-500 mm rainfall), reporting 30-45% reduction in surface runoff and a 20-30% improvement in deep soil moisture infiltration.

title: Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
summary: Highlights that habitat fragmentation and agricultural intensification are primary drivers of terrestrial biodiversity loss; mosaic agricultural landscapes with native vegetative boundaries maintain up to 3x higher arthropod and avian species richness than homogeneous monocultures.
